Lithuanian conservative leader proposes universal conscription from 2030
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:35:00 UTC
20:35:00 KST

Lithuania should introduce universal military conscription from 2030, opposition Homeland Union-Lithuanian Christian Democrats leader Laurynas Kasčiūnas said Tuesday as he registered legislative amendments proposing an overhaul of the country’s draft system.
Kasčiūnas and a majority of the party’s parliamentary group proposed replacing the annual conscription quota and lottery system with mandatory initial military service for nearly everyone on the annual draft list from January 1, 2030.
Under the proposal, young men would be subject to mandatory conscription, while women could serve voluntarily. Exemptions would apply to people excused from service, those granted individual deferments, and certain final-year students and vocational trainees studying for professions in short supply in the armed forces. The option of alternative service would remain.
The Defence Ministry’s draft list for this year included 42,556 young people, of whom 5,000 were scheduled to be called up.
Kasčiūnas said the proposed changes would require a fundamental review of the conscription system to reflect the changing nature of warfare and the military’s staffing needs.
“We propose to conduct a very serious review of the conscription concept, related to the fact that new warfare requires new approaches to drafting,” he said. “Take drone operators, for instance. Perhaps sometimes strong physical training is not required if a clear drone operator training program can be opened.”
He added that the armed forces could adopt more flexible approaches to training personnel for different roles and assess whether everyone needed to serve in barracks under the traditional model.
Kasčiūnas said the priority should be to establish a new system before determining the additional funding it would require.
“We need to start primarily with the system, with the concept of how it should work, and then see how much it might cost,” he said. “I believe we can really move from talk to decisions now.”
If the amendments are adopted but preparations fall behind schedule, the transition period could be extended, he said. However, he argued that lawmakers should approve the legislation and set a hard implementation deadline rather than continue debating the issue indefinitely.
Kasčiūnas acknowledged that the conservatives failed to introduce universal conscription when they headed the government between 2020–2024. However, they adopted amendments allowing more conscripts to be called up and established a military commandant system, which he described as a transitional model that revealed both strengths and weaknesses in the existing system.
“The times and the political situation also require it,” he said, arguing that Lithuania needed to move to a new stage of military preparedness.
Defence officials support expansion
Lithuania’s military leadership has also outlined plans to expand conscription in the coming years.
Chief of Defence Raimundas Vaikšnoras said the armed forces aimed to draft “nearly everyone who is willing and able” by 2030 and increase the number of conscripts to 7,000-8,000 through different forms of military service.
Conscripts currently serve for nine months, although an option introduced this year allows mandatory service to be completed in three, six or nine months.
School graduates aged 18–22 are also being called up, with their numbers expected to increase annually. Some politicians have described the measure as a step toward universal conscription.
In mid-September, the National Universal Defence Coordination Council, chaired by President Gitanas Nausėda, announced that it would propose accelerating the introduction of universal conscription.
Nausėda has said the transition to universal conscription is only a matter of time as Lithuania establishes a national division. Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas has also said the country is moving toward universal conscription but must first make the necessary preparations.
Public support for the proposal appears substantial. A survey commissioned by the Universal Defence association in August found that nearly 80% of the population supported introducing universal conscription, with priority given to drafting men.

Just under 270,000 people on welfare in Switzerland
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:35:00 UTC
20:35:00 KST

Just under 270,000 people on welfare in Switzerland
Just under 270,000 people received social assistance in Switzerland in 2025. The social assistance rate stood at 2.9%, which is in line with the previous year’s figure.
The number of people receiving social assistance thus rose by 4.5% compared with the previous year, as the Federal Statistical Office (FSO) announced on Tuesday. As in previous years, children and young people had the highest rate of social assistance among all age groups, at 4.8%. The FSO noted that the rate decreases steadily with age.
The highest social assistance rates by region were recorded in several cantons in French-speaking Switzerland and in Basel City. Rural cantons in Central and Eastern Switzerland, as well as the cantons of Fribourg, Graubünden and Valais, recorded lower rates. These differences are linked, among other things, to regional economic and demographic structures, as well as to the particular pressures faced by urban centres, the report added.
More
How Swiss welfare works
Single parents
In a separate study published on Tuesday, single parents in Swiss towns and cities are more likely than average to rely on social assistance. This is shown by the key figures report by the Urban Initiative on Social Policy.
In many towns, around a quarter of single-parent households with children under the age of 18 receive social assistance. The risk of poverty for single-parent households is almost five times higher than that for all households.
Many single parents receive social assistance on top of their wages because their earnings are not sufficient to support their families. The report identifies education and training, suitable childcare and supplementary family benefits as effective forms of support.
Every year, the City Initiative compares social assistance figures across 14 cities. Last year, the social assistance rate stood at 3.9%, slightly below the previous year’s figure. Overall, social assistance figures remained stable.

In the northern West Bank, Israeli forces raided the eastern neighborhood of Jenin as well as the towns of Meithalun, Jaba and Qabatiya, arresting at least six Palestinians, according to local sources.

For Pope Leo, there was little choice but to go to Latin America
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:31:03 UTC
20:31:03 KST

For Pope Leo, there was little choice but to go to Latin America
VATICAN CITY, Oct 27 - Since undergoing surgery on October 13 to treat lung cancer, Pope Leo has weighed a major decision: whether to press ahead with an intense, three-country tour of South America just 24 days after having part of one lung removed.
But in the end, according to a biographer and other experts, Leo had little choice but to continue with a visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru as the Vatican announced on Monday, to show he remains up to the job of leading the world's 1.4 billion Catholics.
Leo, 71, was born in the US but spent decades as a missionary and bishop in Peru before becoming pope. He is also devoted to that country, where he became a citizen and which he considers an adopted home.
"Cancelling would have meant … sending a certain message that this (surgery) has been a real rupture in this pontificate," Massimo Faggioli, a papal historian, told Reuters.
"The message is now, 'No, that health crisis is over. And I can do it,'" said Faggioli, a professor at Villanova University, near Philadelphia, where Leo earned one of his diplomas.
Elise Allen, author of a biography of the pope for Penguin Peru, said his decision "shows an incredible determination to continue with the mission that he believes has been entrusted to him by God."
FOREIGN TRIPS NOW INTEGRAL PART OF PAPACY
Travelling abroad has become a major part of the modern papacy, with popes seeking to meet local Catholics, spread the faith, and conduct international diplomacy.
They often draw large crowds, and officials in Argentina have estimated that some seven million people will attend events with Leo over his three days in that country.
Making foreign trips has become an integral part of being pope, said Faggioli. "That has become the real test of the papacy, if you can do exhausting trips or not," he said. "The papacy is … a global job and you have to be there in person."
Leo's November 6-17 South America tour is set to be one of the most intense taken by a pope in decades. He is scheduled to travel some 31,000 km (19,300 miles) over the 10-city tour and give 36 speeches.
The Vatican said on Monday that the pope was fit for the trip, citing Leo's personal physician Dr. Luigi Carbone.
Dr. Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital, said the risks of complications for the pope related to the surgery now appear "quite low."
He said that Leo being cleared to fly by his doctors should indicate that his operated lung has fully expanded and any surgical wounds are healing without signs of infection.
"My primary advice for patients in this situation is not to push themselves too far and to listen to their body when it asks for rest," Liu told Reuters.
"I would expect his team would primarily be watching for any signs of exhaustion" during the trip, said the doctor.
CATHOLICS WILL WATCH TRIP CLOSELY
Leo is recovering from surgery two weeks ago in which doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung to treat lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer.
The pope's doctors said last week that further examinations of the tissue removed in the operation had confirmed the cancer was localized and he would not require any further ongoing cancer treatments.
The Vatican said on Monday the trip would go forward with no changes to the previously planned itinerary, which includes 12 flights and two helicopter trips.
The Vatican press office did not immediately respond to questions about whether there would be any additional emergency planning for the trip or additional medical personnel added to the tour.
"It is very intense and I think the risks are very real," said Allen, the only journalist to interview Leo since his May 2025 election. "But obviously, Leo is confident in how he's feeling and his medical team is confident in what they're seeing."
Faggioli said he expects Catholics across the world will be watching the trip closely, to see how Leo is faring.
"Everyone will look at every speech he gives, every hand he shakes," said the academic. "This decision will keep some people, as we say in Italian, 'sulle spine' (on tenterhooks)." REUTERS

DUBAI – Yemen’s Houthis said they targeted Saudi Arabia’s biggest oil refinery with a ballistic missile on Oct 27, as blasts shook the capital of the world’s top crude exporter.
Saudi Arabia, the Middle East’s largest economy, has suffered weeks of strikes from the Iran-backed Houthis against oil and civilian sites, including Riyadh’s international airport.
“The Yemeni Armed Forces were able to target the Ras Tanura refinery in the Eastern Province with a ballistic missile,” Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X, saying the strike caused “massive fires”.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis earlier said it shot down three missiles fired by the group towards the Eastern Province.
A resident in the city of Al Khobar, south of the Ras Tanura complex, said he heard explosions around dawn and received a text message alert.
“We got the alert on the mobile and then heard a very loud bang,” the resident said.
Maritime security agency Vanguard said a fire was reported in the Ras Tanura area in the early hours of Oct 27 after an attack.
“The fire has reportedly been contained, while the extent of damage and any impact on oil-loading operations remain unclear at current,” Vanguard said.
The Ras Tanura facility, along Saudi Arabia’s Gulf coast, is home to one of the largest refineries in the Middle East and a cornerstone of the kingdom’s energy sector.
The complex has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day. It has been repeatedly targeted by strikes blamed on Iran, including a drone attack in early March that forced a partial shutdown of the refinery.
Meanwhile, a series of explosions echoed across the capital, Riyadh, shaking office windows in the city centre. A text message alert warned residents to seek shelter.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it intercepted two ballistic missiles that were fired at Riyadh.
Egypt ‘declared war’
Earlier, a Houthi official said the Egyptian Parliament’s decision to authorise defensive military support for Saudi Arabia amounted to a declaration of war.
Egypt’s Parliament authorised the measure on Oct 26, following a request from Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.
“It is truly remarkable that while these people go to discuss what they call ‘peace in the region’, Egypt and its Parliament declare support for the so-called defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and in doing so, declare war against the Republic of Yemen,” said Mohammed Ali al-Houthi, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, in a Telegram post.
It was not clear exactly what support was on offer from Egypt, which has the Arab world’s largest military.
Al-Houthi’s statement also pointed to the visit on Oct 26 to Tehran by the Saudi defence minister, Pakistan’s army chief and Turkey’s intelligence chief, in a bid to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East war.
Riyadh, Ankara and Islamabad recently signed a NATO-style defence pact in Mecca, pledging to consider an attack on one country as an attack on all three.
Turkey and Pakistan have not announced any strikes on the Houthis during the group’s weeks of attacks on Saudi Arabia.
‘Not afraid of any alliance’
Al-Houthi said the group was “not afraid of any alliance that may be formed”.
Yemen’s largely dormant conflict reignited in July, further destabilising the region months into the Middle East war between the United States and Iran.
The Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing swathes of Red Sea coastline in a major offensive in September.
The Houthis have, in turn, reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control.
The Houthis ramped up in October attacks on Saudi Arabia, forcing the cancellation of flagship events and shutting down Riyadh’s airport for two weeks.
The Houthis’ war with the Saudi-led coalition began in 2015, months after they ousted the internationally recognised government from the capital Sanaa in September 2014. AFP

Knives, knuckledusters and a ‘Gucci robbery’: police discover chats linked to Milan riots
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:30:49 UTC
20:30:49 KST

A 30-year-old researcher detained over the clashes in Milan has refused to answer a judge’s questions, as police investigating the unrest uncovered chats threatening officers and carried out searches across Italy.
Youssef Siher exercised his right to remain silent when questioned by preliminary investigations judge Tiziana Landoni in Milan’s San Vittore prison on Tuesday.
Investigations into the unrest that rocked the centre of the Lombard capital on 17 and 18 October are proceeding on two separate tracks: messages found by investigators in a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members, and the Milan prosecutor’s inquiry into Siher’s alleged role in organising and spreading content linked to the so-called 17 October Movement.
Chats with threats: “We steal their weapons” and “set fire to a government building”
The Monza and Brianza Digos (General Investigations and Special Operations Division) began investigating after finding a message in a chat in which a user urged others not to put their balaclavas on straight away, to avoid being identified by police.
On 22 October, acting on a warrant from the Milan juvenile prosecutor’s office, investigators searched the home of the teenager believed to have written the message. They found a balaclava and an Under Armour T-shirt thought to have been stolen from a shop looted in Milan. A search of another minor turned up a second T-shirt of the same brand, also believed to have been taken during the looting.
But it was the first boy’s mobile phone that gave investigators their most significant lead, pointing them to a WhatsApp group with more than 230 members. The conversations referred to weapons, knives, smoke bombs and firecrackers, as well as plans to attack officers, snatch their weapons, damage police vehicles and set public buildings on fire.
Messages cited by investigators include “And we steal their weapons”, “Let’s grab one, beat him up and take his weapon” and “Hey guys, if we’re going to protest, let’s set fire to a government building”. Others urged people to get hold of knives, clubs and pepper spray, while some discussed stealing cars and targeting businesses, with references to a “Gucci robbery” and a McDonald’s.
The chats also mentioned further demonstrations planned for 24 October, which risked turning violent. The information gathered helped trigger a nationwide preventive operation.
Knives, knuckledusters and balaclavas: 150 searches
On 24 October, around 150 personal and home searches were carried out in several Italian provinces, coordinated by the Central Directorate of Preventive Police and involving Digos units and Flying Squads from various cities. The main aim was to find illegally held weapons and ammunition.
In Brianza, the checks covered 32 people living in 16 municipalities, including Monza, Seregno, Giussano, Carate Brianza, Limbiate, Nova Milanese and Desio.
Officers seized folding and butterfly knives, a hatchet with “1312” engraved on its blade – a numerical code for the acronym ACAB (“All Cops Are B*****ds”) – knuckledusters, a telescopic baton, two blank-firing pistols missing their red safety caps, glass breakers, balaclavas and other items classed as offensive weapons.
Investigators are continuing to piece together the alleged conduct and identify anyone else responsible.
Siher stays silent
Siher was detained on 24 October and is accused of incitement to commit crimes, aggravated by terrorist intent, and of organised violence during public demonstrations. Prosecutors say he runs the social media channels of the 17 October Movement, which was set up after the clashes in central Milan.
Landoni must now decide whether to validate his detention and grant the request for him to be held in prison pending trial, submitted by chief prosecutor Marcello Viola and prosecutor Francesca Crupi, who attended the hearing. Prosecutors argue there is a risk he could flee or reoffend. A decision is expected by 28 October.
Siher is represented by lawyers Benedetto Ciccarone and Yasmina Abu Sharar, who deny he incited violence or terrorism and have asked for his release.

Büro Ziyu Zhuang designs Chinese museum cluster to "blend seamlessly" into meadow
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:30:00 UTC
20:30:00 KST

Büro Ziyu Zhuang designs Chinese museum cluster to “blend seamlessly” into meadow
Chinese architecture studio Büro Ziyu Zhuang embedded four cultural buildings, including a viewing tower and a rammed-earth workshop, into parkland in Xianning, China, to create the Zi Museum.
Located along Zishan Lake in Xianning, Hubei Province, the project comprises four public buildings designed to complement the guest houses of the Ziyouji resort on the other side of the lake.
The centrepiece of the project is the 3,000-square-metre Zi Museum, which features a multi-faceted, layered structure made from pale concrete and was organised around a central courtyard.
Büro Ziyu Zhuang (BUZZ) created three separate access points into the museum at various levels, to follow the natural elevation of the landscape.
On the ground floor, the museum has flexible gallery spaces and a garden restaurant, with a lower-level entranced located near the main traffic route to make installation setup and collection storage easier.
At the front of the museum, a path from the main building leads to a viewpoint closer to the lake.
Visitors can also go from the viewpoint into the museum’s central courtyard and straight to the viewing ramp onto the museum’s rooftop.
“Visitors who are here for nature viewing are able to bypass the interior gallery space, accessing the rooftop viewing platform directly from the outdoor park, while a different circulation was created for those who are here for the gallery exhibitions,” explained BUZZ.
“This allows serious academic exhibition and relaxed social gathering to co-exist in the same building,” it continued.
BUZZ organised the interiors of the museum as an “open labyrinth”, the studio said.
Galleries, public passages, rest and hospitality areas are intertwined to create a free-flowing viewing experience that was designed to evoke the sense of wandering in a Chinese garden.
Next to the museum sits another viewpoint, described by the studio as a “meditation tower”, which features stairs that circulate around a hollow core at its centre.
These continue underground, where they lead to a sunken courtyard wrapped in metal mesh.
The tower can be used as a viewpoint, as well as for small outdoor gatherings and exhibitions.
The third building, a rammed-earth workshop, was designed to seamlessly embed into the landscape.
Like the museum building, this also has a walking ramp, which leads up to a grass-covered rooftop while slightly revealing the entrance below.
Nearby sits the final building, a bookshop with an overhanging roof design that creates a sheltered entrance facing the main street.
It gently steps down towards the lake, where its glass facade opens up to create views over the parkland and lake.
BUZZ aimed to encourage visitors to explore freely between the four buildings. Rather than designing a set route, the studio wanted to create access to the public art space from every direction of the park.
“The overall project manifests as a continuous, open expansion of green space, which provides the flexibility needed for diverse future operations,” BUZZ said.
“There are no forced axes or rigid zoning between individual buildings; instead, they are connected organically through gentle slopes, undulating lawns, and landscaped pathways, blending seamlessly into the existing meadow,” it continued.
Büro Ziyu Zhuang was founded by architect Ziyu Zhuang in 2016. It now has offices in Beijing, Shanghai and Berlin.
The studio also recently unveiled an UFO-shaped gallery that sinks into grassland in Inner Mongolia, as well as an observatory in China that resembles a “spaceship or alien form”.

Design team: Jian Liu, Churan Li, Yue Liu, Zhendong Chen, Chen Liu, Chen Liang, Wei Cai, Zhuliang Ding, Haoxuan Zhang, Zheng Gao, Peicheng Pan, Jiawen Xu, Yicheng Gao, Ya Wen, Chuanni Peng
Drawings and diagrams: Mengzhao Xing, Zhongqi Ren, Yanhan Xu, Han Yu, Jiaxin He

Iranian, Russian universities explore potential to boost co-op

Iranian, Russian universities explore potential to boost co-op
TEHRAN - Iran’s Persian Gulf University and Russia’s Novosibirsk State University have discussed ways to strengthen scientific cooperation and expand joint research initiatives.
During an online meeting, the two universities outlined their respective capacities, explored potential areas of collaboration, and agreed to examine mobility programs involving industry participation in both countries.
Persian Gulf University initiatives are primarily focused on three strategic areas of excellence: energy, petroleum, gas, and petrochemistry; marine studies; and international business and commerce. By prioritizing these areas of scientific knowledge and academic activity, Persian Gulf University aims to strengthen its constructively important role in establishing and maintaining peaceful coexistence and sustainable development, as well as enhancing human prosperity and well-being in the Persian Gulf region.
The university’s internationalization project has begun in recent years, and there has been significant growth in the international indicators, including the number of international academic members, international students, and international events. The university’s mission is to become a third-generation international university with excellence in science, technology, and entrepreneurship to respond to the surrounding society’s needs and create value for society, develop competent citizens, and perform its social roles.
Persian Gulf University has an excellent reputation for teaching quality, academic research, and graduate employability. Admission is limited to students who pass the national entrance examination administered annually by the Iranian Ministry of Science, Research, and Technology.
Novosibirsk region is home to one of Russia’s most prominent universities—a symbol of the research-oriented university model in Siberia—situated in the heart of the science city, Akademgorodok.
Relying on high-quality education, fundamental research, and close collaboration with institutions of the Russian Academy of Sciences, the university holds a distinguished position within the country’s science and technology system.
The combination of a dynamic academic environment, an international scholarly community, and a focus on basic sciences and advanced technologies has established it as a key center for cultivating the next generation of scientists and innovators—both in Russia and globally.
Tehran, Moscow set to establish joint science and technology commission
Iran and Russia are preparing to establish a joint commission on science and technology, with a document on international scientific cooperation between the two countries set to be signed at a meeting of the commission.
In September, Ehsan Qaboul, head of the Ministry of Science, Research and Technology’s Center for International Scientific Cooperation, said Iran is firmly committed to expanding ties with Russia, outlining the next steps by Tehran and Moscow to strengthen bilateral cooperation, including the formation of the joint science and technology commission.
Qaboul added that the Minister of Science, Research and Technology is scheduled to travel to Moscow within the next three months to finalize the document on international scientific cooperation between Iran and Russia.
He also announced plans for 500 cooperation programs with Russian universities and scientific institutions.
The programs include holding 100 joint educational courses involving Russian professors, enabling 100 doctoral and master’s students to choose a second academic supervisor from among professors at
Russian universities, and organizing 100 technology events aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation from science and education into the technology sector.
Qaboul further said that 100 joint cultural events with Russian universities and academic and educational institutions, as well as 100 scholarships for Russian students, are also among the planned initiatives. The scholarships will give priority to students seeking to study Persian language and literature.
The official also stressed Iran’s support for Persian-language programs at Russian universities, saying Iranian professors are ready to teach Persian to Russian speakers either in person or online.
In June, Iranian Science, Research and Technology Minister, Hossein Simaei-Sarraf, and Russian Science and Higher Education Minister, Valery Falkov, reviewed strategies for developing scientific, educational, and academic cooperation between the two countries, with an emphasis on expanding professor and student exchanges, strengthening research cooperation, and facilitating academic interactions.
Simaei-Sarraf considered the development of Russian language chairs in Iranian universities and Persian language chairs in Russian universities as a sign of deepening scientific and cultural ties between the two countries.
Falkov, for his part, pointed out the beginning of a new university admission period in Russia and the welcoming of Iranian students to study at the country’s universities, emphasizing the importance of providing employment opportunities and utilizing the academic potential of graduates after their return to Iran.

The most haunted hotels in Europe you can book a stay in this Halloween
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:28:41 UTC
20:28:41 KST

From heartbroken lovers to airmen who have fallen to their untimely deaths, these hotels on the continent have guests with no respect for the 11am checkout time.
A spectre is haunting Europe. No, hang on. Spectres are haunting Europe, and apparently people are willingly sleeping in the same space as them.
While I personally would avoid any hotel that claims to be haunted, there are a number of properties across the continent that loudly and proudly shout about their paranormal guests, and with Halloween coming up, we thought it was time to spotlight them.
Here’s where to stay if you want a truly haunted Halloween experience.
Golden Fleece, York, UK
Billing itself as one of the most haunted cities in Europe, practically every street in York has a building with a ghost story attached to it.
The Golden Fleece, a pub on Pavement, claims to be the most haunted in the city, and for those who aren’t satisfied with just enjoying a pint among the spectres, you can also book a night in one of the rooms here.
According to York’s tourism board, paranormal guests you might encounter during your stay include Lady Alice Peckett, the wife of the pub’s owner from the early 18th century, and a British airman who fell out of a window here in 1944.
The Ancient Ram Inn, Gloucestershire, UK
Originally built in the late medieval period, The Ancient Ram Inn has had plenty of time to rack up supernatural figures that wander its halls while guests sleep.
Its owners say it’s the most haunted bed and breakfast in the UK, with some 20 ghosts, including a young girl named Rosie, reports Metro. One ghost hunter even claims to have encountered a female sex demon. Blimey.
The Shelbourne, Autograph Collection, Dublin, Ireland
When it comes to five-star hotels, you tend to have certain expectations: Top-notch service, fantastic bars and restaurants, and preferably a nice wellness area with a spa or swimming pool.
You probably don’t expect to run into the mischievous spirit of a seven-year-old girl named Mary Masters who died of cholera in 1791.
But that’s exactly what you’ll get at The Shelbourne, Autograph Collection in Dublin, according to the Irish Mirror, with sightings as frequent as two or three times a week.
Actress Lily Collins even claimed to have seen the ghost during a stay here while filming The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones.
Hotel Union Øye, Norway
While Mary Masters is supposedly limited to the sixth floor of The Shelbourne, the ghost said to be inhabiting Hotel Union Øye sticks to “The Blue Room”.
The tale goes that a servant girl named Linda started an illicit affair with one of Emperor Wilhelm’s officers, and The Blue Room was where the pair would meet.
It ended in tragedy. Unable to divorce his wife and be with the woman he loved, the officer killed himself. Linda, not wanting to live without him, killed herself by walking into the lake, never to be seen again.
Now, according to Norway’s tourism board, Linda’s ghost is said to be heard weeping in The Blue Room.
Toftaholm Herrgård, Sweden
Another broken-hearted ghost can be found at Toftaholm Herrgård in Sweden.
Servant Mats fell in love with the daughter of a count, who was promptly married off to the son of a nobleman. Upon discovering the news, Mats hung himself in one of the guest rooms of the mansion.
Describing him as a “gentle ghost”, the team behind Toftaholm Herrgård say guests claim to have seen him appearing behind women staying in the hotel, occasionally putting his hand on their shoulder.

Family Physician Program being implemented in 64 medical networks nationwide
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:27:26 UTC
20:27:26 KST

Family Physician Program being implemented in 64 medical networks nationwide
TEHRAN – The health ministry is implementing Family Physician Program in 64 medical networks across the country, providing services to some 3.5 million individuals in the initial phase, and diagnosing new cases of patients with diabetes, hypertension, and pre-diabetes.
Around 13.6 million people are currently covered by the program, including 7.7 million in urban areas and the remainder in rural areas, IRNA quoted Alireza Raeisi, an official with the health ministry, as saying.
Noting that the rural population has been fully assigned, the official said that the process of assigning individuals to Family Physician Program in the urban population is being completed, and urban coverage will expand with more physicians joining the program.
Around 2,528 physicians are operating in rural and urban pilot centers, and some 1,610 specialists will soon start providing essential services to the patients, he added.
Referring to the development of digital health infrastructures, Raeisi said integration of systems at different levels of service, the connection with insurance systems, the scheduling of appointments, the referral of patients, and the creation of management dashboards are parts of the adopted measures.
According to the official, some 408,000 referrals to higher health services, about two million prescriptions, and 753,000 medical tests have been recorded so far.
Up until now, 19,246 new cases of diabetes, 34,731individuals with high blood pressure, and 9,322 individuals with prediabetes have been diagnosed, amounting to 49 and 37 percent of expected target population with hypertension and diabetes, respectively.
The official went on to say that the subsequent phases of the program will include breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening tests, disease risk assessment, hearing screening tests, child care, identification of overweight and obesity, and childbearing counselling.
In July, the third phase of the Family Physician Program and referral system kicked off on July 28 in 19 cities, Alireza Raeisi, an official with the health ministry, said.
The program aims to make treatment referrals more concentrated and provide more convenient access to health services.
Successful implementation of the Family Physician Program is essential to the health system. There are no other options; the failure to implement the program would inflict the greatest damage on the health system, IRNA quoted Raeisi as saying.
“Over 100 countries worldwide have implemented the program, and an analysis of global experiences indicates that its full implementation is not feasible in the short term; rather, it requires developing a supportive culture, careful planning, patience, perseverance, and continuous follow-up. Nevertheless, based on existing experiences, we assess the program’s implementation process in the country as positive and promising,” Raeisi highlighted.
Referring to the implementation of the program in Fars and Mazandaran provinces, the official said that the unsuccessful experiences in these provinces resulted from improper implementation rather than a failure to fully implement it. Hence, the precise and principled implementation of the current program is of great importance.
The new phase of the program should be implemented in some cities, like Firouzabad, Jahrom, Larestan, Fasa, and Jouybar, in which previous phases of the program were implemented, to ensure its efficiency, he noted.
Drawing upon the experiences of the first and second phases, the implementation of the third phase should be pursued with enhanced speed, precision, and quality. Furthermore, the chancellors of the universities and the heads of the colleges should continuously oversee the selected networks, regularly monitor the implementation process, and collect necessary feedback. They will also need to consider the Social Determinants of Health (SDH), Raeisi further noted.
The rural family physician program started in 2005. Back then, it also targeted villages and cities inhabited by fewer than twenty thousand individuals to make treatment referrals more concentrated and provide more convenient access to health services, ISNA reported.
Periodic examinations and monitoring of people’s health status, easy and round-the-clock access to basic services and primary care, and frequent visits to doctors are the characteristics of a family physician.
Medical, dental, mental, midwifery, nutrition, laboratory, pharmaceutical, and medical imaging are among the services offered by the program.
Based on the Family Physician Program, a physician and a midwife offer services in rural areas; every 3,300 villagers have a physician, and there is a midwife per 5,200 people in villages.
The program will gradually target other parts of the country as well, ISNA quoted Health Minister Mohammad-Reza Zafarqandi as saying.
“It is a large-scale program based on social behavior change. Designing new patient pathways, reforming the referral pattern, and improving the healthcare network system requires careful coordination between the Health Ministry, governors, and other relevant institutions at the provincial level,” IRIB quoted Zafarqandi as saying.
So, it is essential to develop a national headquarters headed by the President to oversee the overall management of the program, he added.

302,000 Russian soldiers killed or wounded by Ukrainian drones since January, Defense Ministry says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:25:09 UTC
20:25:09 KST

302,000 Russian soldiers killed or wounded by Ukrainian drones since January, Defense Ministry says
Units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces have killed or severley wounded 302,000 Russian servicemen by using drones since January 2026, the Ukrainian Defense Ministry said on Oct. 27.
"Each defeat is recorded on video in the Delta combat system and verified by the Brave1 defense innovation cluster," the Defense Ministry said.
The Ukrainian military uses an incentive system in which the verified destruction of enemy personnel and military materiel awards combat units points that they can exchange for more drones, electronic warfare equipment, and other gear on an internal marketplace.
In September, 46,230 Russian soldiers were killed or irrecoverably wounded, according to figures published by the Ukrainian General Staff.
Of these, 32,739 were killed or wounded by drones, the figures show, amounting to about 70% of the total.
The highest number of casualties Ukrainian drones inflicted on the Russian military was recorded in March, with almost 34,000 soldiers killed or irrecoverably wounded.
Drones of various types now cause the vast majority of casualties on both sides. "The destruction of enemy manpower using UAVs helps preserve the lives of Ukrainian soldiers, making it difficult for the enemy to approach our positions," the ministry said.
The prevalence of drones from both sides has significantly changed assault tactics, making heavy equipment such as tanks a rare sight on the battlefield.
With the "kill zone" reaching 20 kilometers (12.4 miles), Russia has largely stopped using tanks or other heavy equipment for assault operations, Joint Forces Task Force spokesperson Viktor Trehubov said on Sept. 20. Drones have replaced many of the tanks' roles for both sides, since a tank driving close to the front would be easily spotted and hit by much cheaper drones.

The threat looming over Sweden: how the country is preparing for a possible war and learning from Ukraine
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
13:25:00 EET
20:25:00 KST

The threat looming over Sweden: how the country is preparing for a possible war and learning from Ukraine
Sweden's support for Ukraine is unprecedented. The governing coalition and opposition are united in their political backing, and the public is wholeheartedly rooting for Ukraine to win. Blue and yellow flags are visible throughout Stockholm, solidarity events take place regularly, and Ukrainians can use public transport free of charge. With the February aid package included, Sweden's total military assistance to Ukraine has reached SEK 128 billion (over €11 billion).
However, as tensions escalate in the Baltic region, concern is growing within Sweden itself. At a meeting with journalists in Stockholm, Ukraine's Ambassador to Sweden, Svitlana Zalishchuk, highlighted the persistent cyber threat to Swedish infrastructure.
Sweden regularly records incursions into its airspace by Russian fighter jets and the presence of Russian submarines near key maritime routes. Espionage is also becoming an increasingly pressing concern: suspicious individuals are more frequently seen photographing and filming critical infrastructure. Stockholm recognises that these are not isolated incidents, but part of Russia's broader preparations for hybrid warfare.
This is precisely why Sweden relies on its unique concept of Total Defence, which was officially reintroduced in 2015, following Russia's annexation of Crimea and the start of its aggression in Ukraine's east.
Every state agency and local authority has a clearly defined protocol to follow if the situation escalates. Emergency preparedness drills are compulsory for all organisations, with no exceptions, and are held annually. The country also regularly tests its mass alert system. I happened to hear it last summer while visiting a friend in Uppsala. The siren has an unusual, low, muffled sound, somewhat like the distant rumble of heavy lorries.
In a crisis, national radio will serve as a vital link between the state and the public. Sweden's official preparedness leaflet, In case of crisis or war, which is distributed to every home by the Swedish Civil Defence and Resilience Agency, lists a battery-powered radio among the essential items people should keep at home. It is Sveriges Radio (P4 channel) that has been designated as the official source of emergency information, which will continue broadcasting even in the event of a total blackout or a communications collapse.
Sweden's public broadcaster is now looking closely at how Ukraine has managed to keep broadcasting throughout the war. At meetings with Sveriges Radio's management, including Director-General Cilla Benkö and her deputy, Gabriel Byström, the focus was on practical solutions: ensuring newsrooms can operate without a reliable power supply, keeping broadcasts on air during bombardments and protecting journalists from burnout.
Commercial media outlets are not lagging behind either. Fredrik Malmberg, head of news at TV4, one of Sweden's largest television networks, said the channel has drawn up several contingency plans for wartime operations – right down to setting up backup offices for teams in the event of an attack on its main broadcasting facilities.
Sweden set up its own Psychological Defence Agency in 2022 to counter disinformation and study hostile information campaigns and psychological operations. In collaboration with Fojo Media Institute, the agency provides specialist training for professional journalists. Leading editorial offices, meanwhile, have been designated as high-alert facilities.
Ukraine remains a prominent subject in Swedish media outlets, regardless of their political leanings. Aftonbladet, one of Sweden's leading centre-left newspapers, published an op-ed with the telling headline "A Russian victory will cost twice as much as aid to Ukraine", openly urging the government to commit at least 1% of GDP to supporting Ukraine and to invest in its victory, not merely its survival.
Meanwhile, Isobel Hadley-Kamptz, a columnist for the respected centrist newspaper Dagens Nyheter, takes aim at Donald Trump in her article "Trump has always wanted Russia to win", accusing him of playing into Moscow's hands. She argues that pressuring Kyiv to make territorial concessions would threaten the security of Europe as a whole – a danger Sweden is well aware of.
During off-the-record meetings, we kept being asked the same questions: how to work as a journalist during a full-scale war, how to retain people in the profession and keep them alive, and how to deal with the challenges we face. The measures Sweden is taking now will undoubtedly help its society withstand the worst-case scenario.
Yet, looking at Sweden's peaceful, thriving streets, I had just one thought: I would not wish on anyone in the world what Ukraine is going through.
	
The trip to Stockholm took place as part of the Women Leaders in Media programme, organised by the NGO Women in Media with backing from International Media Support (IMS).
Khrystyna Golovko

Iran joins Coalition of Action to Recover Endangered Species
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:24:53 UTC
20:24:53 KST

Iran joins Coalition of Action to Recover Endangered Species
TEHRAN – Iran has officially joined the Coalition of Action to Recover Endangered Species (CARES), which aims to strengthen international cooperation to preserve and restore the country’s wildlife.
The CARES was unveiled at the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP17) in Yerevan on October 16. Colombia and Armenia launched the initiative with 17 founding participating governments: Armenia, Belize, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Fiji, Indonesia, Madagascar, Mexico, Panama, Papua New Guinea, Peru, United Kingdom, and Vanuatu. Iran has become a member of the coalition as the 18th country.
The coalition is supported by the Reverse the Red Action partnership as secretariat.
The membership document was signed by Hamid Zohrabi, deputy head of the Department of Environment (DOE), on Monday.
Speaking at a meeting on this occasion, Zohrabi underlined the need for equitable distribution of resources and technology to save endangered species.
Iran’s name will be listed on the website of the coalition as a country that has developed action plans for the conservation of 40 wildlife species to benefit from technical, scientific, and financial support from CARES.
Some organizations have come together to commit more than $500 million over the next five years to prevent extinctions and recover the world’s most threatened species.
On the sidelines of COP17, Zohrabi and Vivek Menon, chair of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Species Survival Commission (SSC), discussed ways to strengthen cooperation in developing management and conservation programs for endangered species.
The talks particularly focused on conservation and restoration programs for the Asiatic cheetah, the great bustard, and the Persian zebra, onager, their respective habitats, as well as the reintroduction of the Persian fallow deer into its natural habitats.
Both parties also discussed enhancing technical and scientific cooperation and providing funding under sanctions.
Menon expressed hope that ongoing collaboration between IUCN officials and Iranian experts would guarantee the survival of endangered species, such as the Asiatic cheetah, in Iran.
COP17 is being held under the framework of the Convention on Biological Diversity, alongside the Twelfth meeting of the Parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (CP-MOP-12) and the Sixth meeting of the Parties to the Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits Arising from Their Utilization (NP-MOP-6).
The two-week negotiations are being held in two stages: technical-level discussions followed by the ministerial segment.
The leaders’ summit took place on October 16, featuring an address by President Masoud Pezeshkian. It marked the first time a president of the Islamic Republic of Iran had attended a Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
Addressing the summit, Pezeshkian called for “peace diplomacy” to protect biodiversity, condemning the devastating environmental impact of wars of aggression as ecocide and urging the international community to establish effective, transparent and enforceable mechanisms to safeguard natural heritage during wartime.
According to the latest report by the IUCN Red List, about 154 vertebrate animal species and around 25 percent of plant species in the country are at risk of extinction, with 117 species being classified as critically endangered in the national list. Persian zebra, Asiatic cheetah, black bear, great bustard, and yellow deer are among animals that are in danger of extinction.
Among extinct animals, the Hyrcanian tiger and Persian lion are the two feline species that have disappeared forever in the country. Fortunately, the Persian zebra and the Persian yellow deer are examples of successful conservation efforts where scientific measures and local community participation have resulted in the species’ recovery.
Genetic map for endangered species being developed
The DOE is developing a genetic map of endangered wildlife species to increase their chance of survival, create a breeding plan, manage their population, and address the risks facing them in their natural habitats.
Effective conservation of endangered species is almost unattainable without a precise understanding of population genetics. To this end, genetic and molecular studies of key wildlife species in the country have been put on the agenda, ensuring that management decisions are based on accurate scientific data, IRNA quoted the head of the National Museum of Natural History and Genetic Resources, Leila Ezzeddinlou, as saying.
Preserving genetic diversity within and between populations, preventing declines in effective population size, avoiding inbreeding and genetic erosion, conserving genes adapted to diverse environmental conditions, and providing genetic resources for species restoration, propagation, and introduction or reintroduction programs are among primary objectives of these studies, she added.
Referring to three research agreements signed between the DOE, the College of Agricultural and Natural Resources of the University of Tehran, and Gorgan University, the official said that as part of the cooperation, a project is underway to investigate the genomic diversity and phylogeny of Levant viper and Latifi’s viper populations, employing conservation and therapeutic approaches based on genomic markers.
Moreover, the development of genetic profiles and maps for the Asiatic cheetah, black bear, and Persian yellow deer, as keystone and threatened species, has kicked off.
The other part of the agreements focuses on the assessment of genetic variation, inbreeding, and kinship relationships within the Persian zebra population, which is being conducted in collaboration with Yazd’s provincial DOE department. The initiative plays a key role in managing small populations and preventing the loss of genetic biodiversity, she highlighted.

On the evening of October 26, a federal judge in the United States temporarily barred the Trump administration from cutting down additional trees or closing the public East Potomac Golf Course, which the U.S. president intends to upgrade to championship standards. UNN reports this, citing Politico.
Details
In her lengthy and sharply worded ruling, Judge Ana Reyes found that the U.S. president’s public statements contradicted the administration’s claims in court that the removal of more than 400 trees earlier this month was routine maintenance, rather than preparation for the president’s grand vision for the East Potomac Golf Course.
"Rarely, if ever, has the U.S. Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," she wrote. "And yet, here we are."
What preceded this
A conservation group and two local residents asked the court to ban further tree removal after the U.S. Department of the Interior cut down more than 400 trees within a short period earlier this month.
Earlier this month, Reyes criticized the administration for cutting down the trees and expressed skepticism toward the government’s arguments in court that it was part of a longstanding plan to clear the historic golf course.
Following a tense hearing, the administration asked the judge—who was appointed by the Biden administration—to recuse herself from the case, citing bias. She rejected the request.
Trump has commented on the case several times, including announcing on social media that the golf course would close on November 15 for a 15-month renovation.
Which golf course is at issue
East Potomac Golf Course is the most prominent of the three public courses owned by the U.S. National Park Service (NPS) in Washington. Last year, Trump seized them, accusing the nonprofit National Links Trust of failing to pay rent, even though the NPS had allowed the nonprofit to offset the rent by investing in golf-course repairs.
The 106-year-old golf course, owned by the National Park Service, is part of Trump’s broader efforts to leave an architectural mark on the nation’s capital, alongside a new White House ballroom and a proposed triumphal arch.
But those efforts have been slowed by fierce lawsuits examining the limits of presidential power.
What’s next
On Monday, Reyes said the government must notify the court 10 days before closing the course or making "irreversible changes".

Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:23:19 GMT
20:23:19 KST

Netherlands pulls out of Eurovision again over Israel participation
- Published
The Netherlands has pulled out of next year's Eurovision Song Contest, with public broadcaster NPO citing "sensitivities" over Israel's participation - reversing a previous decision to take part.
The Netherlands and four other countries boycotted this year's event, after Dutch network Avrotros pulled out.
Avrotros said it would also not take part next year, but NPO, which oversees public broadcasting in the country, stepped in and pledged last month that the country would return in 2027.
However, NPO's media director Jurre Bosman said on Tuesday that "Israel's participation elicits various reactions in society and causes discussion and division", and NPO "has decided to forgo participation in 2027".
'Take a step back'
NPO chair Jet de Ranitz said the organisation had held discussions with broadcasters about participating next year.
"In those discussions, we initially felt there was sufficient support to return. Unfortunately, we were unable to find a suitable format for this.
"As a result, we must conclude that it is currently too early to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest in 2027.
"Due to the sensitivities surrounding the themes currently at play, we have decided to take a step back for the time being."
NPO acknowledged that some Dutch fans may be disappointed, but that the contest would still be aired in the Netherlands.
Eurovision Song Contest director Martin Green said he was "deeply sorry" that the Netherlands would not take part, but added that "we understand their decision, and we respect the strength of feeling behind it".
Green added that organisers recognise that opinions about the contest "differ widely, both within countries and between them", adding: "We do not dismiss any of those views.
"At the same time, we believe the Eurovision Song Contest matters in a divided world. It is one of the few moments each year when people from across Europe and beyond come together around music, creativity and shared experience.
"That spirit of unity is what the contest has always stood for, and we are committed to protecting it."
Green said they looked forward to welcoming a Dutch entry again when they "feel the time is right".
Bulgaria beckons
The Netherlands, Iceland, Spain, Ireland and Slovenia all bocotted the 2026 contest over Israel's participation, amid criticism of its military actions in Gaza and the Middle East.
Eurovision organisers have announced a number of changes in an attempt to address the divisions, including to exclude any country involved in an armed conflict from hosting the competition, and changes to the voting.
As well as the Netherlands, Ireland will also not take part in 2027, and the head of the Spanish public broadcaster has come out in favour of a boycott.
The Czech public broadcaster has also pulled out, but cited spending cuts as the reason.
Eurovision 2027 will take place in Burgas in Bulgaria on 15 May, following Dara's win in Vienna this year with the dance track Bangaranga.

EU countries to receive EUR 4.7B in reimbursement for aid to Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:20:00 UTC
20:20:00 KST

EU countries to receive EUR 4.7B in reimbursement for aid to Ukraine
This was reported by the EU Council press service, according to Ukrinform.
“These decisions mark a major step towards implementing the political agreement reached by EU member states on 25 September 2026 to mobilise €6.6 billion for Ukraine under the EPF,” the press service said.
The package also provides an additional €230 million in funding for the EU Military Assistance Mission in support of Ukraine (EUMAM Ukraine).
The agreement included the provision of €1 billion in new military aid to Ukraine and further reinforcement of EUMAM Ukraine in 2027
It is recalled that, following the latest decisions, the EU’s total support for Ukraine under the EPF has reached €10.8 billion. This amount includes €9.9 billion to reimburse the cost of military assistance provided by member states and €950 million for military training under the EUMAM mission.
The European Peace Facility was established in March 2021 to finance activities under the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP). In particular, the EPF allows the EU to finance measures aimed at strengthening the defense and military capabilities of third countries, as well as regional and international organizations.
To date, the EU has provided Ukraine with €6.4 billion in support through the European Peace Facility. On September 25, 2025, EU member states agreed to mobilize a total of €6.6 billion, of which €4.9 billion was allocated through the Council decisions adopted today. The EU has also allocated €3.5 billion – extraordinary revenues generated from frozen Russian assets (so-called windfall profits) – through the European Peace Facility to address three of Ukraine’s priority needs: ammunition, air defense and drones. At the same time, military equipment worth more than €1.5 billion was procured directly from Ukraine’s defense industry.

Why should Big Tech know what you’re working on? Scale AI accused of spying on AI trainers
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:19:00 UTC
20:19:00 KST

The European Centre for Digital Rights, known as Noyb, is filing complaints against San Francisco-based startup Scale AI over the way its training platform Outlier tracks its 900,000 workers.
A prominent European data protection group said it was filing five legal complaints in Europe against American startup Scale AI over the way its training platform Outlier tracks its workers, infringing on their rights.
It comes as AI companies face increasing scrutiny in Europe, with the EU’s AI Office opening investigations into OpenAI and Anthropic this month. In the US, meanwhile, President Donald Trump signed an agreement with the six largest American AI firms allowing them to regulate themselves, a sign of growing divisions over how to govern the technology globally.
There are also growing concerns worldwide that AI could take people’s jobs and be used for harmful purposes.
The European Centre for Digital Rights, known as Noyb, is filing two complaints in Austria, one in France, one in the Netherlands and another in Italy, it said in a statement published on Tuesday 27 October, relating to the way workers are trackers and the lack of protections granted by its freelance contract model to recruit staff.
Scale AI’s Outlier AI platform recruits freelancers and subject-matter experts to help train, evaluate and improve artificial intelligence models, using a platform worker model like those used by Uber and food delivery services.
According to Noyb, the platform uses more than 900,000 freelancers to evaluate and correct the responses of AI systems, with customers including Meta, OpenAI, Google and the US government, which the organisation describes as a process in which workers are “effectively giving their expertise to US Big Tech companies”.
Outlier "collects huge amounts of personal data and forces workers to go through an invasive biometric verification to earn money", the NGO said.
"In Europe, this far-reaching workplace surveillance clearly violates the workers’ fundamental right to data protection," it said.
Noyb alleges that while workers are on the Outlier platform, trackers from companies such as TikTok, LinkedIn and Facebook are placed on their devices and given access to their personal data.
This includes IP addresses, contact details and data that can be used for targeted advertising and profiling, the group said.
“Such constant and extensive tracking while working really goes against all reasonable expectations. Why should LinkedIn or Facebook know which tasks you're working on?” said Lisa Steinfeld Leiser, Data Protection Lawyer at Noyb.
It also alleges that Scale AI forces workers to repeatedly go through a biometric verification process carried out by a company called Persona, which includes making video recordings of their face and uploading their ID.

Shortage of Arabic ballot papers reported in Israel elections
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
11:17:50 UTC
20:17:50 KST

Breadcrumb
Shortage of Arabic language ballot papers reported in Israel elections
Palestinian citizens of Israel have reported shortages of Arabic-language ballot papers at several polling stations during Tuesday's parliamentary elections, prompting a rights group to demand urgent intervention over concerns that Arab voters are being denied equal access to the vote.
The Haifa-based Adalah Legal Centre for Arab Minority Rights said it had received complaints from voters and election observers since polling stations opened on Tuesday morning, reporting the absence of Arabic-language ballot papers in several Arab towns and mixed cities.
The complaints came from Baqa al-Gharbiyye, Haifa, Nazareth, I'billin, Eilabun, Shefa-Amr and Nof HaGalil, according to a statement issued by the organisation.
Adalah subsequently sent an urgent letter to the head of Israel's Central Elections Committee, demanding that Arabic-language ballot papers be supplied immediately to all affected polling stations and that clear instructions be issued to election officials.
The organisation warned that the shortages undermined the right of Palestinian citizens of Israel to participate in elections on an equal footing.
It stressed that Arabic is the mother tongue of hundreds of thousands of eligible voters and that providing ballot papers in the language is essential to ensuring fair and accessible elections.
Rami Haidar, media coordinator for the Joint List, told The New Arab that most reported shortages had occurred in mixed cities, where Palestinian and Jewish residents live alongside one another.
"We are in contact with the relevant authorities to resolve this problem," he said.
Arab party alleges systematic attempts to obstruct voting
Separately, the United Arab List (Ra'am) filed a formal complaint with the Central Elections Committee, alleging a systematic campaign to obstruct voting for the party.
The party said the alleged interference included the arrest of several campaign activists, the disappearance of its ballot papers and the deliberate destruction of voting slips in several Arab communities.
According to Ra'am, Israeli police arrested several prominent party activists in the Negev early on Tuesday, including Sayyaf Abu Riyash from Rahat, Hussein Masoudin from Shaqib al-Salam and Ibrahim al-Quraibi from the village of al-Sirr, along with others.
The party said the arrests had taken place without any clear justification.
Ra'am also reported widespread shortages of its Arabic-language ballot papers, marked with the letters "ع م", in several towns, including Nazareth and Shefa-Amr.
It said torn ballot papers had also been discovered, raising suspicions that they had been deliberately damaged.
The party urged supporters to check that their ballot papers were available and undamaged, and to demand replacements immediately if they found any missing or defective slips.
Ra'am accused Israel's right wing of seeking to weaken its electoral strength and prevent it from securing eight seats in the Knesset, which it said could obstruct the formation of an alternative government led by the opposition's "change camp".
"Your vote is your power, so do not give it up," the party told supporters.
Meanwhile, the Joint List issued video messages explaining that voters might encounter two versions of its ballot papers at some polling stations.
One version carries text in both Arabic and Hebrew, while the other is printed in Hebrew only.
The party stressed that both versions were valid and could be used to vote.
It urged supporters to ensure that their ballot papers were free of markings or damage and matched the officially approved versions.
The Joint List also called on Palestinian citizens to turn out in large numbers, presenting the election as an opportunity to defeat the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition partners, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.

Across China: Researchers propose new irrigation to balance water conservation, food security in China
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
19:17:46 CST
20:17:46 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- A new study shows that China may better balance water conservation, food security and investment returns by adopting more efficient irrigation strategies, and expanding irrigated farmland only where conditions are optimal.
The study, published in the journal Nature Food, was led by researchers at the Institute of Atmospheric Physics (IAP) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Hohai University and Xiamen University, in collaboration with several other Chinese and international institutions.
As rising temperatures and droughts put more pressure on food production systems, irrigation is becoming more important for farmers adapting to climate change. But expanding irrigated farmland further burdens already limited water supplies. The researchers therefore look for ways to save water, protect cereal production and improve investment returns all at once.
The team examined 42,190 county-level agricultural statistical records, 3,576 household socioeconomic survey responses and 2,230 irrigation technology comparison trials. It also focused on China's three staple crops: maize, wheat and rice.
The study found that China's agricultural irrigation underwent a significant technological transition between 2010 and 2022. In 2010, earthen-channel water delivery and flood irrigation were still widespread. By 2022, these inefficient practices had declined substantially, while water-saving technologies had become more common. However, the pace of change varied widely across crops and regions.
Wang Jinxia, a professor at Hohai University in east China's Jiangsu Province, said upgrading irrigation and water-saving technologies has long been a key part of China's farmland water conservancy investment.
Wang explained that at the current rate of technology adoption, irrigation water use per area for the three staple crops is projected to fall by only 9.4 percent to 16 percent by 2030. This projected reduction would fall short of the 25.5 percent water-saving target set by the national agricultural sustainable development plan for 2015 to 2030. The plan sets a cap of 373 cubic kilometers on national agricultural irrigation water use by 2030.
The study showed that deploying the most efficient irrigation technologies across all existing irrigated areas could more than meet the water-saving target. However, even such widespread upgrades would not be enough to offset possible crop yield losses caused by future climate change, posing risks to food security.
The researchers therefore proposed a new approach: first improve water-use efficiency in existing irrigated areas, and then, within water resource constraints, use the water saved to convert some rainfed farmland into irrigated farmland. The strategy aims to reduce the adverse effects of future climate change.
The study also found different optimal strategies for the three crops. For maize, the preferred approach is to adopt more advanced irrigation technologies while moderately expanding irrigated areas. For wheat and rice, less expansion is needed, and medium-efficiency water-saving technologies in newly developed irrigated areas could be enough to ensure food security under future climate conditions, meet water-saving policy targets and maximize investment returns.
Zhang Tianyi, a senior scientist at IAP, said the real question policymakers need to answer is which crops need irrigation, where irrigated area should be expanded, by how much, what technologies should be adopted and whether the investments are economically viable.
He noted that previous studies had largely focused on projecting changes in irrigated areas without fully accounting for interactions among irrigation technologies or between existing and newly developed irrigated areas.
"By integrating multi-source data and developing a new analytical framework, the study aims to provide more actionable scientific evidence for these specific investment decisions," he said.
The researchers emphasized that irrigation is not the only solution. Agricultural production is also influenced by crop variety breeding, cultivation management, land management scale and other factors. Irrigation investment should therefore be coordinated with the development of stress-tolerant crop varieties, climate-resilient cultivation practices and the construction of high-standard farmland.
Chen Huang, a researcher from Xiamen University in east China's Fujian Province, said the study drew on three independent datasets collected through different survey and research approaches. Despite their different sources, the model was able to capture the decline in agricultural irrigation water use and the improvement in irrigation productivity in China over the past decade.
"Future research will further incorporate agricultural policy and economic factors such as farmland consolidation and changes in agricultural commodity prices to refine the assessment of irrigation investment," he said. ■

Researchers in Australia find potential new treatment for rare genetic disorder
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
19:17:43 CST
20:17:43 KST

MELBOURNE, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Researchers in Australia have discovered a way to release a genetic "brake" that silences healthy genes in Prader-Willi syndrome, opening a potential new path to treating the rare genetic disorder.
Researchers at Australia's Walter and Eliza Hall Institute of Medical Research (WEHI) found that removing a protein called SMCHD1 lifted the genetic "brake," allowing healthy but dormant genes to switch back on, according to a WEHI statement released Tuesday.
In Prader-Willi syndrome, the protein switches off certain genes essential for development and brain function, contributing to developmental delays, intellectual disability and an insatiable appetite that can lead to obesity. About 400,000 people worldwide live with the condition, the statement said.
The study, published in Science Advances, used CRISPR gene-editing, stem-cell and genomic technologies to examine the effects of removing SMCHD1 in patient-derived cells and animal models.
Current treatments mainly address symptoms rather than the underlying cause, often relying on multiple medications, surgeries and specialist care, providing limited relief, the researchers said, adding that potential new therapies targeting the cause of Prader-Willi syndrome are now advancing through a WEHI spinout company. ■

Feature: Lively celebrations mark end of Buddhist Lent, boat racing festival in Laos
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-27
19:17:43 CST
20:17:43 KST

This photo taken on Oct. 26, 2026 shows an illuminated boat along the riverbank in Vientiane, Laos. (Photo by Kaikeo Saiyasane/Xinhua)
VIENTIANE, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- In Laos, riverfronts come alive with glowing floating lights, bustling crowds and festive sounds as people gather to celebrate the end of Buddhist Lent and the boat racing festival, an occasion that brings together religious traditions, community spirit and vibrant festivities.
The end of Buddhist Lent, which falls on Oct. 26 this year, begins with religious observances as people rise early to visit temples, give alms and offer food to monks as a way of making merit.
In the evening, crowds gather along riverbanks to float decorative banana-leaf boats adorned with flowers, candles and incense sticks. The offerings are released onto the water as a gesture of respect for the river and, for some participants, a symbolic way of washing away bad luck.
For Channapha Khamdy, a 29-year-old resident of Lao capital Vientiane, the festival is an occasion not to be missed. "This is one of the most important festivals. Everyone should experience it at least once in their life," she told Xinhua.
This year, Channapha brought Thai and Chinese friends she had met while studying abroad to the Mekong Riverbank to experience the celebrations firsthand. "They flew to Vientiane just to attend the festival," she said.
Proud to share her country's traditions with her friends, Channapha highlighted the candlelight processions, lantern displays and illuminated fireboats along the riverbanks as must-see highlights of the celebration.
"Even though it is crowded, I still want to bring my friends out to experience the atmosphere for themselves. I believe these memories will stay with them even after they return home," she said.
In many parts of Laos, the end of Buddhist Lent is followed by traditional boat racing festivities. In Lao capital Vientiane, the boat racing festival, held on Tuesday, also provides an opportunity for local vendors to sell their products while visitors experience Lao culture through traditional goods, local food and festive activities.
Sommanivanh, a 42-year-old woman from southern Laos' Champasak province, came to the Mekong Riverfront with her family, drawn by the variety of products on display and the lively atmosphere surrounding the celebration.
"This is one of my favorite festivals of the year. I never miss the celebration," she said.
Sommanivanh also shared her impressions of this year's festivities, noting that she had seen more young people wearing traditional clothing, visiting temples and strolling around the festival. She described the trend as a positive way to showcase Lao culture and traditions to foreign visitors while helping preserve the country's cultural heritage.
The festival is not only an occasion for people to enjoy festivities around town, but also a time for families and friends to come together at home.
"Since my house is near the Mekong River, it is a tradition for me to welcome friends from near and far. We gather to eat, drink and celebrate together," Bee, a Vientiane resident, told Xinhua.
He added that during the festival, friends and visitors often come to his home carrying food and drinks to share, turning the occasion into a gathering filled with warmth and friendship.
"For us, it is a way to come together and strengthen our bonds, so that we do not grow distant from one another. That is one of the most beautiful things about the celebration," he said. ■

People float decorative banana-leaf boats along the riverbank in Vientiane, Laos, Oct. 26, 2026. (Photo by Wang Yuping/Xinhua)

KUALA LUMPUR, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) - Malaysia's median monthly wage for formal-sector employees rose 4.8 percent year on year to 3,000 ringgit (734 U.S. dollars) in June 2026, official data showed on Tuesday.
The number of Malaysian formal-sector employees increased 3.3 percent to 7.20 million in June from 6.97 million a year earlier, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said in a statement.
Male employees accounted for 55.1 percent of the total, or 3.97 million, with a median monthly wage of 3,000 ringgit. Female employees made up the remaining 44.9 percent, or 3.23 million, earning a median wage of 2,964 ringgit.
Malaysia's formal labor market remained stable and resilient in the second quarter of 2026, supported by continued growth in formal employment and median monthly wages, DOSM said. (1 ringgit equals 0.24 U.S. dollar) ■
